Resolves #18863

🌿 *Tab has always handed the arrow keys a cell to move from; after this, Enter cannot end an edit and leave them with nowhere to start.*

A double-click edit committed with Enter left the grid with **no selected cell at all** — the cell carried `class="neo-grid-cell"` and nothing else — so the arrow keys had no anchor and the next keystroke went nowhere. Tab never had this hole: it selects the cell it moves to.

Evidence: L2 (component tier, real pointer and keys) → L2 required (both ACs are DOM-observable). Residual: none.

agent-preflight: not hosted here (Brain-only); the PR baseline jobs run in CI. Change class: `defect` (`fix`).

## Deltas from ticket

- **The selection goes in `onEnterKey`, not `completeEdit()`.** `completeEdit()` is the single commit terminal, which makes it the obvious home and the wrong one: Tab (`onTabKey`) and a re-activation (`startEdit`) also call it, and **both go on to select a cell of their own**. Selecting the edited cell there would be immediately superseded — a second worker round trip for a selection nothing ever sees. The fix belongs to the terminal that ends the edit *in place*.
- **The invalid-draft AC needed no fix, only witnesses.** Three of its four gestures already held and none of those three was armed. An AC about behaviour holding is not met by behaviour that happens to hold — an unarmed terminal can be changed silently.
- **A measured asymmetry, asserted rather than smoothed over.** The click-away gesture keeps the editor in its own cell with its rejected draft and starts no second edit — but focus lands on the **View**, where Enter and Tab leave it in the input. The arm asserts what was measured. The focus half of that behaviour belongs to #18927.
- **A state I asserted that the fixture cannot reach.** The focus-leaving arm first asserted the cell reads `Name 5`. It reads `Required`: the editor is still embodied, so the cell shows the editor, not a value — and Escape does not help, because the click put focus outside the grid so no key reaches the editor. The arm now reads what is observable.
- **Escape is left without an anchor, knowingly.** The AC says *commits*, and Escape cancels. The same "nowhere to arrow from" gap exists after Escape; recording it as a decision rather than an oversight.

## The AC-1 attempt, and why it is #18927's

Worth recording, because it cost a lane and produced a defect-note. #18898 merged during this work, so `onBodyRender()` — *"the one place where an embodiment can go"* — reached `dev`, and it is the right seam: @neo-fable handles embodiment *lost*, the reprojection-focus AC handles it *regained*. **The first half works**: a suspended editor takes focus back, and `CellEditingPooling.spec.mjs`'s explicit `page.locator(INPUT).focus()` becomes unnecessary — a workaround sitting in the suite, the same tell as #18862's `retype` helper.

**⚠️ Corrected after merge — the paragraph that stood here was wrong, and it is worth leaving the correction rather than the claim.**

I wrote that the second half had "no sound signal", on this probe:

```
PROBE-CF {"viewId":"neo-grid-view-2","viewContainsFocus":true,"activeId":"grid-cell-editing-outside"}
```

— and concluded that `containsFocus` stays true for a move to a non-Neo element, filing an unowned engine defect-note. **@neo-opus-grace reproduced it and the conclusion is the opposite:** the flag goes `true` → `false` **within 150 ms**, 3/3, from a suspended edit and a plain one, and `setComponentFocus` sets the flag *and* fires `focusLeave` in the same call. There is no engine defect; the note is retracted.

**My probe read the flag one gap too early.** `containsFocus` lives in the App Worker, DOM focus changes on main, and I read synchronously after the click — capturing the value from before the round trip. The number was real, the moment was wrong. The discipline is stated in `component/grid/CellEditing.spec.mjs`'s own docblock, which I had open all day: *never assert an absence right after an event; drive a later event with a visible effect and read once that has landed.*

So the reverted AC-1 work was **one line** from correct: I evaluated `view.containsFocus` inside `onBodyRender` and deferred only the `focus()` call to `editor.on('mounted', …)`. The guard belongs **inside** that mounted callback, which is where @neo-opus-grace's #18927 design puts it. Reverting was still the right call at the time — shipping the working half would have weakened the criterion to *"takes focus back"* and dropped the clause that makes it safe — but the reason I gave for it was not the true one.

Nothing in this PR's own diff depends on any of that; this section was context for the criteria that moved to #18927.
